newsitem.title: USA: FDA approves Immunex prostate cancer drug.
newsitem.headline: FDA approves Immunex prostate cancer drug.

text.p: Immunex Corp said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared its lead chemotherapy drug, Novantrone, for marketing in combination with steroids for the treatment of pain related to hormone refratory prostate cancer.
The approval makes Novantrone, which is already on the market as a treatment for leukemia patients, the first chemotherapy drug approved for advanced prostate cancer.

The company said Novantrone in combination with steroids significantly reduces pain in about 40 percent of patients and is generally well tolerated. That success rate is considered significant since prostate cancer, in its most advanced form, is one of the more difficult cancers to treat.
Many late-stage prostate cancer patients have responded poorly to other forms of chemotherapy because they are often elderly men with other medical problems and limited bone marrow reserve.
Because Novantrone is already on the market, Immunex has set up a toll free number to provide information about the new application.

Immunex said a majority of patients who have advanced prostate cancer eventually progress to a hormone resistant form of the disease, in which hormones fail to stall its progression. The main symptom of this form of prostate cancer is severe, sometimes debilitating pain.
The American Cancer Society estimates there will be a total of 317,000 new cases of prostate cancer in the U.S. in 1996 and 41,400 deaths, Immunex said.
